source_location: main.pdf p. 2730, Fig. 9 (hydrogen excess adsorption, 25 °C), series CX16AOXI, highest-pressure marker (14th of 14 markers incl. origin); volumetric capacity from p. 2731 Fig. 11a 'Adsorbed hydrogen', highest-pressure marker

The lower three curves of Fig. 9 are nearly coincident; markers of the other series are partly hidden. Table 1 values are per total sample mass (Ni included); carbon-mass basis (Table 4): S_BET 1775 m2/g, W0-N2 0.72, W0-CO2 0.40 cm3/g. 0.2 at% Ni by XPS; Ni grain size 2.7 nm by XRD. purification_method: after KOH activation washed with 5 M HCl, then distilled water until pH of drained solution reached 6
activation_method: KOH chemical activation, activating agent/precursor mass ratio 4, wet impregnation, 750 °C under N2, 2 h
functional_groups: carboxylic acid, phenol, carbonyl, quinone groups (CO2/CO TPD of the HNO3-oxidised support; PZC 4)
source_location: main.pdf p. 2731, Fig. 10b 'Total hydrogen' (filled triangles), marker at about 20 bar (marker 8 of 10 incl. origin); volumetric capacity from Fig. 10a 'Total hydrogen' (filled squares)
notes: Digitized: archive: fig10b_total_77K.json. Volumetric capacity (g H2 per L, 1 L tank, includes compressed gas) digitized: 20.0499 bar, 24.8758 g/L, archive: fig10a_total_77K.json. Total = adsorbed + compressed gas in the voids of the packed sample, computed by the authors from the excess isotherm (Vs = 1 - rho_e/rho_r); same run as I5. Origin marker (0 bar) counted in isotherm_point_count but not extracted. Temperature printed as 77 K (Sec. 2.7) and −196 °C (captions). Table 1 values are per total sample mass (Ni included); carbon-mass basis (Table 4): S_BET 1774 m2/g, W0-N2 0.71, W0-CO2 0.46 cm3/g (label printed CX45OXS in Table 4). Ni not reported by XPS; Ni grain size 2.3 nm by XRD. W0-N2 = DR wide-micropore volume (N2, −196 °C), stored in micropore_volume_cm3_g; W0-CO2 = DR narrow-micropore volume (CO2, 0 °C), stored in micropore_volume_co2_cm3_g; VT calculated from the N2 isotherm at saturation; dp = DFT mean mesopore size from the N2 adsorption branch (the 16 or 45 nm in the label). Before the H2 isotherm the sample was activated 2 h at 400 °C in H2 (100 cm3/min) and degassed in situ at 150 °C under vacuum before and after that treatment (duration and end pressure not stated). Paper does not state which laboratory made the H2 measurements; corresponding author's group used.
basis_evidence: The total hydrogen storage capacity of an adsorbent which can physisorb hydrogen in a tank with a given volume is the sum of the capacity obtained by adsorption and the amount of gas stored by compression in the existent voids; Fig. 10 - (a) Volumetric hydrogen storage capacity (total and adsorbed) of sample CX45AOXS and the amount of hydrogen storage by compression at −196 °C and pressure up to 40 bar and (b) gravimetric storage capacity (total and adsorbed) of sample CX45AOXS
measuring_lab_id: Zubizarreta group, Instituto Nacional del Carbón, CSIC
